headline: Graph, hypergraph and language-model embeddings predict drug response, synergy and resistance
label: Graph And Language Models For
summary: New graph and language-model methods target drug response, synergy and miRNA-drug resistance prediction, alongside gene and sequence embedding tools.
synthesis: The dominant thread is relational and representation learning for pharmacological outcomes. MulDR preserves omics-specific cell-line relations for drug response prediction, MTDKF fuses metapath topology with domain knowledge to predict miRNA-drug-disease resistance and sensitivity triplets, and GLH2Syn combines global diffusion with structure-aware local views in a heterogeneous hypergraph for drug synergy. A second strand applies language-model embeddings to biological sequence and gene function: GeneEmbedLLM uses Longformer attention and contrastive learning for gene embeddings, and LESS-PseU fuses DNABERT2 embeddings with handcrafted features for pseudouridine sites. The peptide toxicity framework MBFGNK similarly fuses protein language model, 3D structure and hypergraph features. What is new is the multi-view fusion of structured topology with pretrained embeddings; the items do not all address cancer outcomes directly.
